# How Can I Monitor Feed Stock and Consumption by Herd?


You monitor feed by recording purchases and daily distribution by herd, calculating consumption per animal and the remaining stock in days, and alerting the team before supplies run low. On **Jestor** , this runs through a feed **table** , distribution **Forms** , and calculated fields.


Feed is often the largest cost in livestock. Running out disrupts production, while overfeeding wastes money, and without records, it is hard to know whether consumption matches the animals' needs.


## What untracked feed costs


- Feed shortages that hurt production
- Overfeeding that wastes money
- No view of cost per animal or per liter or kilo produced
- Purchases made late at higher prices
- Differences between herds that nobody notices


## How feed monitoring works


- Each feed type is a **record** with stock and cost
- Daily distribution is logged by herd
- A calculated field shows consumption per animal and days of stock left
- Alerts appear when stock approaches a minimum


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Supply is planned instead of improvised
- Feed efficiency can be compared between herds
- Costs per animal become clear
- This scales from a small farm to a large feedlot or dairy


Feed managed by eye Feed stock and consumption tracked


Shortages and waste Days of stock and cost per animal visible


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Can workers record distribution from a phone?** Yes, through a mobile form. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can I compare cost per animal between herds?** Yes, dashboards can group by herd.


**Can I be alerted when stock is low?** Yes, automation can notify the manager.
